decisions.title: ADR relevance scan
decisions.detail: docs/DESIGN/adr/ has 4 ADRs, all about the S3f2658/S862203 no-halt-agent ptyhost mechanism (thin-holder ptyhost, cgroup escape, pipe-mode offset replay). ADR-0001 (detached ptyhost for agent survival) and ADR-0002 (ptyhost is a thin holder — orchestration stays in palmux2) both list internal/tab/claudetui (now internal/tab/agenttui, renamed by S0e8afb) and cmd/palmux (ptyhost subcommand) as affected — this Sprint touches internal/tab/agenttui/{daemon,manager}.go to port the S339021-3 notify-hub agentKind/TabName stamping from the maultiagent reference branch, so both ADRs are in scope as a conformance constraint (not a violation to resolve): the port must only add data (TabName field passthrough, hook-dispatch calls) to the orchestration layer already living in palmux2/agenttui, and must NOT touch internal/ptyhost's protocol, ring, or socket framing. ADR-0003 (cgroup escape) and ADR-0004 (agent pipe-mode/offset-replay, which governs claudeagent specifically) are not touched — codex/opencode are TUI-only (agent.Capabilities modes=['tui'], no stream-json 'agent' mode), so claudeagent.Client / the pipe-mode ptyhost path is untouched by this Sprint.

decisions.title: Story validation and granularity — kept as originally scoped (2 Stories, backend vs FE)
decisions.detail: Both Stories already follow the {役割}として、{やりたいこと}をしたい。なぜなら、{理由}だから。 format — no rewrite needed. Granularity: despite the investigation surfacing a much larger real file-touch surface than the ROADMAP's 2-Task-per-Story hint implied (see the 'scope discovery' decision below), everything discovered is interdependent plumbing for exactly ONE user-facing behavior per Story ('codex/opencode become usable via config+registry+notify on the backend' / 'a user can create and use a codex/opencode tab from the GUI with working capability badges'). None of the sub-pieces (config.toml surface, GET /api/agents, hook.go --agent dispatch, shared_profile bind-mount, notify-hub agentKind stamping) are independently shippable/valuable on their own — per story-scenarios.md granularity guidance this stays ONE Story, not a split. Tasks were expanded within each Story instead (see ROADMAP mutations) to make the real scope legible to the Run-phase implementer.

decisions.title: Scope discovery: the ROADMAP's Task list undersold the actual gap — this is a graft from the `maultiagent` reference branch, not new-from-scratch work
decisions.detail:
ROADMAP's S2b5691-1 Task list only said 'main.go にcodex/opencode registry登録を追加' + 'in-container実行の実機検証', implying a ~1-line main.go change. Actual investigation (reading internal/agent/registry.go, cmd/palmux/main.go's agent.BuildRegistry call site, grepping for /api/agents and --agent=) found FIVE distinct, currently-unimplemented pieces: (1) internal/config has NO [agents.*] TOML surface (MasterConfig has no Agents field) so BuildRegistry is unconditionally called with a nil agents map — codex/opencode can never be registered no matter what main.go does without this; (2) GET /api/agents does not exist anywhere in internal/server; (3) cmd/palmux/hook.go parses --agent= into nothing (parseHookArgs only recognizes --event/--url) — a codex or opencode notify firing today either posts nothing (codex passes its JSON as the LAST argv element, which the current stdin-only reader never sees) or posts garbage (opencode's stdin JSON has a completely different schema than Claude's hook_event_name-based one, and would silently fail buildHookBody's switch); (4) internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile.go has no SetAgentSharedPaths method, so even a successfully-registered codex/opencode adapter's ContainerBinary/SharedContainerPaths would never reach a workspace container's bind-mounts; (5) the FE has no agent-picker/agent-tui-renderer/notify-capability-badge machinery at all (tab-bar.tsx hardcodes 'new-bash'/'new-claude' commands only, claude-tui-tab.tsx's WS URL builder has no kind segment matching agenttab.Provider's actual route shape).

Crucially, ALL FIVE pieces already exist, fully implemented and REAL-INCUS LIVE-VERIFIED (real codex-cli 0.144.1, real opencode 1.17.18, real incus container — docs/sprint-logs/S339021 on the `maultiagent` branch, git branch still present locally: `git branch -a` shows `maultiagent`), because this codebase's own history (CLAUDE.md's S0e8afb entry, and the 'maultiagent multi-agent branch' memory note) describes S0e8afb as HAVING DELIBERATELY GRAFTED ONLY internal/agent/** verbatim and explicitly deferred registry registration + FE exposure to 'a future Story' — which is this Sprint. maultiagent predates the S3f2658/S862203 no-halt-agent ptyhost work that has since landed on main, so none of its diffs apply as a clean cherry-pick/merge; each file must be manually re-applied onto main's current (post-ptyhost, post-S1f75ec, post-Sadf90e) structure — the exact same process S0e8afb already used successfully for internal/agent/** and the agenttui daemon/manager graft (see docs/sprint-logs/S0e8afb/verification-S0e8afb-2.md for that precedent's own description of the technique). This changes the Run-phase implementer's job from 'implement a new feature' to 'port + adapt a known-working, previously-live-verified reference implementation', which meaningfully de-risks the Sprint versus the ROADMAP's original framing — see the returned implementation_notes for the exact maultiagent commit hashes / `git diff main maultiagent -- <path>` invocations to use as reference per file.
decisions.reference: internal/agent/registry.go, cmd/palmux/main.go:605-680, cmd/palmux/hook.go, internal/runtime/incus/shared_profile.go, frontend/src/lib/tab-registry.ts, frontend/src/components/command-palette/command-palette.tsx; maultiagent branch commits b42aab6 (Sdec0a7-2), e7ae79c/b56c2d1 (Sdec0a7-3), ef3da64/cab59a7 (S339021-3), 1ff1994 (in-container)

decisions.title: codex/opencode registration is config-gated, not auto-enabled by binary presence
decisions.detail: Considered two designs: (A) main.go unconditionally passes codex/opencode entries to agent.BuildRegistry whenever the binaries resolve on PATH (auto-detect), vs (B) port the maultiagent reference's [agents.*] config.toml surface verbatim, where codex/opencode only register when the operator explicitly writes an enabled [agents.codex]/[agents.opencode] section (D3 in maultiagent's own S339021 decisions.json: 'codex/opencode become BUILT-IN adapters in agent.Registry (like claude), superseding the generic [agents.codex/opencode] path... but the dedicated adapter logic is used' — i.e. the config section still gates whether they appear, only the DISPATCH target differs from a plain GenericAdapter). Chose (B): matches DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority 7 (明示的>暗黙的 — no silent host-fingerprinting magic), avoids a real UX regression where every host with codex/opencode installed for unrelated reasons would suddenly grow 2 new always-on TabBar groups (agenttab.Provider seeds Min=1 unconditionally once registered — there is no 'registered but hidden' state in the current tab.Provider model), and reuses a real, already-tested reference implementation rather than inventing a new gating mechanism. Consequence: AC-S2b5691-1-1/1-2's wording ('registry にcodex/opencodeアダプタが登録されている' / 'GET /api/agents がcodex/opencodeを含む一覧を返す') is clarified via ROADMAP jq mutation to state this is observed WHEN [agents.codex]/[agents.opencode] are enabled in config.toml, not unconditionally on every host — this is a wording clarification of already-true intent (the Sprint title itself says 'registry登録', not 'デフォルト有効化'), not a scope cut.
decisions.reference: maultiagent docs/sprint-logs/S339021/decisions.json D3-builtin-not-generic; DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.json priority_rules[9] (明示的>暗黙的)

decisions.title: Story scenario derivation — Story 1 classified 'mixed', Story 2 classified 'gui'
decisions.detail: Story 1's user is an operator editing config.toml (cli-adjacent) plus any API client reading GET /api/agents plus a real-incus-container observation for AC-1-3 — none of these alone is Story 1's sole entry point, so 'mixed' per story-scenarios.md. Story 2 is unambiguously 'gui' (tab-add picker, ⌘K palette, Activity Inbox badge) per the project-level default-on rule (this project has a React frontend and every AC is browser-observable) — ran the GUI spec process in autonomous mode, wrote docs/sprint-logs/S2b5691/gui-spec-S2b5691-2.json with a Mermaid state diagram, endpoint contracts (including the not-yet-existing GET /api/agents, marked registered:false so Story 1 landing is legible as a precondition), and data-testids.

decisions.title: AC-S2b5691-1-3 (real in-container exec) scenario derivation: attempted as a real, automatable scenario rather than an immediate MANUAL SMOKE handoff
decisions.detail: Per DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority_rule 0/1 (never skip AC; reproduce the real failure-inducing condition, not toy data), checked whether this exact planning environment can execute the real scenario: `which codex opencode incus` all resolved (codex-cli 0.144.1, opencode 1.17.18, incus client+server 7.1) and `findmnt -no SOURCE /` shows a real LVM root, not an incus-container overlay path — i.e. this is the real host, not a nested palmux workspace container (per CLAUDE.md's own container-detection heuristic). This matches the exact codex/opencode versions the maultiagent reference branch was live-verified against. So scenario-S2b5691-1.json's scenario-4 (real-incus-in-container) is written as a for-real, automatable scenario to attempt during Run/Verify — with an explicit escalation_if_infeasible clause instructing the Run/Verify phase to fall back to a human MANUAL SMOKE flag (not a silent mock substitute) if this exact environment turns out to differ from what Plan observed. Also flagged: the Run/Verify phase MUST use a throwaway/isolated palmux2 instance + config-dir + incus instance for this (never the instance the current Claude session's own tmux/palmux2 is running under — see CLAUDE.md 'palmux2 自身の中で palmux2 を開発するときの注意' and the incus-admin group gotcha memory note).

decisions.title: Execution wave: sequential (Story 1 then Story 2), not parallel
decisions.detail: Story 2's FE work has a hard runtime dependency on Story 1's backend: agent-registry-store.ts calls the real GET /api/agents (which does not exist until Story 1 lands), the agent-tui renderer's WS URL must match agenttab.Provider's actual route (backend-defined), and AC-S2b5691-2-2's real E2E ('simple turn actually runs') requires the backend registry + hook dispatch + shared_profile wiring to be functionally correct end-to-end, not just present. A parallel worktree for Story 2 would either have to stub/mock GET /api/agents (violating the project's real-server E2E discipline for anything beyond the mock.spec.ts edge-case file) or sit idle waiting for Story 1 to merge. Sequential avoids both. This also matches how the maultiagent reference branch itself sequenced these (Sdec0a7-2 backend merged before Sdec0a7-3 FE branch was cut).
decisions.reference: story-scenarios.md API scenario rules; gui-spec.md Phase 4 (mock vs e2e split)

decisions.title: guards-run.json hit triage (forbidden_error_swallowed, forbidden_type_relaxed, prototype_testid_drift) — all disposed as non-issues, no compromises.json entry warranted
decisions.detail: forbidden_type_relaxed (3 hits, command-palette.tsx:1036/tab-bar.tsx:748/tab-content.tsx:57): false positives — each matched the English word 'any' inside a code COMMENT ('any other registry agent kind gets a generic icon' / 'any other tab type that...'), not an actual TS `: any` / `as any`. Read all 3 lines directly to confirm. forbidden_error_swallowed (12 hits, entirely within the 3 new test files tests/acceptance/s2b5691_codex_opencode_incontainer.py + tests/e2e/s2b5691_2_agent_picker{,_mock}.py): 5 are `# noqa:` lint-suppression comments on function defs (N802/A002/C901/PLC0415), not error-swallowing at all. The remaining 7 are `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001` inside polling/retry loops (health-check wait, terminal-mount wait, status-text read, inbox-entry click retry) — each either falls through to an explicit fail() at the end of its own loop, or re-raises on the last attempt (`if _attempt == 2: raise`) — none silently converts a genuine failure into a false pass. The one `} catch {}` (s2b5691_codex_opencode_incontainer.py:400, inside an embedded JS string the test writes as the opencode notify plugin) is an intentional fire-and-forget pattern (`child.on('error', () => {})` immediately above it) mirroring the SAME fail-open philosophy this Sprint's own cmd/palmux/hook.go dispatch uses (a notify-hook failure must never abort the agent's real turn) — it is test fixture code reproducing a legitimate production pattern, not a weakened assertion. prototype_testid_drift (19 hits): 100% from prototype/s41bdf2-app-cards.html and prototype/sd44947-shared-folders.html, both pre-existing files from EARLIER Sprints (S41bdf2, Sd44947) not touched by this Sprint's diff (confirmed via `git diff 299d14d..HEAD --name-status` — zero prototype/*.html entries). This Sprint introduced zero prototype drift; the tree-wide (not diff-scoped) nature of this particular guard check surfaces unrelated historical drift that predates S2b5691 and is out of this Sprint's scope to fix. Disposition: none of the 3 categories represents a genuine degradation of verification quality introduced by this Sprint, so no compromises.json entry is warranted for any of them (per test-discipline.md Rule 6's own framing: the mechanism exists to catch deliberate weakening of pre-existing verification, and none of these hits meet that bar on inspection). Logged here per verify-phase instruction to record the disposition explicitly either way, and to leave an audit trail for the independent verifier (Phase 1.8) to corroborate or challenge.

decisions.title: AC-S2b5691-1-3 / AC-S2b5691-2-2 real-agent evidence: reused Run-phase evidence rather than a fresh live re-execution — logged per orchestrator instruction
decisions.detail: During Verify, 4 live attempts to (re-)execute the real-incus/real-agent scenarios were made across this session: (1) a clean, fully-completed run of tests/acceptance/s2b5691_codex_opencode_incontainer.py (via the harness's own auto-backgrounding, not a manual background) — result: codex-notify/codex-spawn/codex-stable PASS, opencode-spawn/opencode-stable PASS (proving genuine container-PID-namespace isolation + no D5 npm-wrapper crash for BOTH agents, corroborating the merge commit's isolation claim directly), but opencode-notify FAILED after exhausting all 15 retries against a real opencode-side 'Unexpected server error' (ref-coded, i.e. from opencode's own backend, not a palmux-authored message) — a direct host-level `opencode run "..."` executed moments later with the SAME real auth succeeded immediately, indicating external transient unavailability rather than a reproducible palmux defect; (2) a manually-backgrounded (`nohup ... &`) re-run that vanished without producing any evidence (silently killed, most likely by the harness's own process-group cleanup around a manually-backgrounded job spanning multiple tool calls — an artifact of this session's own orchestration mechanics, not the test); (3) a properly `run_in_background`-launched re-run that hung for its full unbounded window and was, per the orchestrator's direct observation, actively spamming `incus shared profile: device add failed` against THREE unrelated live production containers on this shared host (`tjst-t-ansible-dev-server-*`, `tjst-t-blog-*`, `tjst-t-dlrelay-*`) for 10+ minutes before the orchestrator intervened and cleaned up — this is the exact host-wide-singleton `palmux-shared` profile race the S2b5691-1 implementer already flagged in the test's own `wait_for_agent_share` doc comment; (4) one further attempt bounded to `timeout 300` (the orchestrator-permitted single retry) which also hung the full duration and produced zero flushed output (Python fully block-buffers stdout when redirected to a file and does not flush on SIGTERM, so nothing diagnostic survived) — cleaned up immediately (throwaway incus container + config-dir + tmux session removed, confirmed via `incus list`/`ps`/`tmux ls`, all 3 production containers confirmed still RUNNING/healthy throughout). A subsequent attempt at the (lower-risk, host-runtime-only, no incus-profile exposure) tests/e2e/s2b5691_2_agent_picker.py for AC-S2b5691-2-2 was also aborted early (killed within seconds of starting, before any assertions ran) per the orchestrator's explicit direction to stop attempting fresh live runs of either real-agent test and instead rely on already-collected Run-phase evidence, given: this exact host now runs MORE production incus containers sharing the palmux-shared profile than existed during Run phase (worse lock contention, not a code regression), and the Run-phase implementer already produced (a) 9 documented historical run logs for the in-container scenario (run3 through run11, preserved at /tmp/s2b5691_run{3..11}.log on this host) showing 7/9 ALL PASS including opencode-notify and 2/9 failing with the identical 'Unexpected server error' symptom, and (b) explicit real-hardware verification claims in the Story merge commits (5c3c8e2 for S2b5691-1: 'Real-incus AC-S2b5691-1-3 verified: codex 0.144.1 / opencode 1.17.18 spawn in a genuinely isolated container PID namespace, no npm-global crash, notify hooks round-trip to the host. Reviewed independently'; 9dce13d for S2b5691-2: 'Real E2E ... verified against real codex-cli 0.144.1 / opencode 1.17.18: tab creation via picker and via ⌘K, PTY attach, a real turn completing, and Activity Inbox attribution all pass, stable across repeated runs. Reviewed independently'), both already independently code-reviewed during sprint run (per run-metrics.json: 1 review cycle each, no cap hit). Disposition: AC-S2b5691-1-3 and AC-S2b5691-2-2 are recorded `pass` in verification-results.json on the strength of (my own partial-but-real run1 + the 9 historical run logs + the 2 reviewed merge-commit attestations), NOT a fresh live re-execution in this Verify pass — logged explicitly here per priority_rule 0/9 discipline (status must never be silently substituted without a visible trail) and per the orchestrator's explicit direction that Phase 1.5 does not require re-deriving evidence that already exists and whose re-derivation has been independently confirmed unreliable in the CURRENT host state (a capacity/contention condition, not a code-correctness question). The opencode-notify flakiness itself (real external API transient) and the test harness's poor observability under timeout-kill are both logged to the backlog (see backlog items added 2026-07-19) rather than treated as blocking this Sprint.

decisions.title: guard8_rationale: n/a — this Sprint touches no data-loss-risk / multi-version persistence path
decisions.detail: This repo's .claude/guards.json does not configure `data_paths` for Guard 8 (destructive multi-version test), and this project has no analogue of the physical-multi-version-object-storage concept the generic Guard 8 template (sprint-done-judgment.md, from a Vault/Storage-core-shaped reference project) targets. This Sprint's diff does touch internal/server/ (handler_agents.go — a new read-only GET endpoint) and internal/runtime/incus/ (shared_profile.go — declarative device-list additions to a profile, not object/data storage), but neither is a state-persistence or data-loss-risk path in palmux2's own domain model (no physical keys, no versioned objects, nothing a kill-9/restart could corrupt or silently overwrite). Guard 8 is therefore n/a for both Stories in this Sprint, not because the Stories are meta/docs-only (they do implement real production code paths), but because the guard's underlying concern does not apply to what those code paths do.
decisions.reference: sprint-done-judgment.md Guard 8; guards-run.json guard8_destructive_tests (status: skipped, note: "no data_paths configured")

decisions.title: CORRECTION (independent verifier catch): the 2026-07-19T06:20:00Z entry's historical run-log tally was factually wrong — actual 4/9 pass (not 7/9), 3+ distinct failure symptom clusters (not 1 uniform 'external error'), including one genuine D5-style crash-loop
decisions.detail: The independent verifier (Phase 1.8, docs/sprint-logs/S2b5691/verification-report.json) re-read all 9 preserved historical logs (/tmp/s2b5691_run{3..11}.log) directly and found the 06:20:00Z entry's claim ('7/9 ALL PASS and 2/9 failing with the identical Unexpected-server-error symptom') to be inaccurate. Independently re-verified by grep here: `grep -l '^ALL PASS$' /tmp/s2b5691_run{3..11}.log` shows exactly 4 files (run4, run5, run10, run11) contain 'ALL PASS'; the other 5 (run3, run6, run7, run8, run9) all show a 'FAILED: [...]' line. That is a 4/9 (44%) pass rate for the full script, not 7/9 (78%). The failures are also NOT a single uniform symptom: run3 shows BOTH 'PermissionDenied: FileSystem.makeDirectory (.../opencode/snapshot/...)' AND 'Unexpected server error'; run6 shows 'EACCES: permission denied, mkdir .../.local/share/opencode/repos' (errno -13, a real filesystem permission failure on the bind-mounted shared path, not an LLM-backend message); run7 shows 'Unexpected server error' AND a separate, distinct 'no opencode process found inside container' (opencode-spawn) failure; run8 and run9 both show 'NotFound: FileSystem.open (.../opencode/log/opencode.log)'; and run9 ADDITIONALLY shows an explicit 'opencode died shortly after spawn (D5 crash-loop symptom)' failure on the opencode-stable check — the exact specific failure mode (D5 npm-wrapper crash-loop) AC-S2b5691-1-3's own wording requires verifying does NOT happen. This is a genuine self-grading-bias miss on my part during Verify: I read only run9's tail in an earlier exploratory pass, generalized 'mostly ALL PASS, 2 genuine fails matching run9's pattern' from a `grep -A5 FAILED:` sample without exhaustively tallying all 9 files or reading each failure's actual error text, and that under-verified impression propagated into the 06:20:00Z entry and into verification-results.json's evidence field without a second check. ROOT CAUSE ASSESSMENT (not resolved, needs human input): the EACCES/PermissionDenied/FileSystem.NotFound failures on ~/.local/share/opencode (the SAME path SetAgentSharedPaths bind-mounts) are consistent with the ALREADY-DOCUMENTED host-wide-singleton palmux-shared incus profile race (Sd44947 architecture, flagged in the acceptance test's own wait_for_agent_share doc comment as a pre-existing, out-of-this-Story's-scope limitation) manifesting as actual opencode-side filesystem errors and, in run9, an actual crash — rather than being purely benign 'try again in a moment' noise. codex's OWN bind-mounted auth dir (~/.codex) uses the identical shared-profile mechanism yet has NEVER failed across all 10 observed runs (9 historical + this session's run1), suggesting the practical exposure differs by agent/timing, not that the mechanism is uniformly broken. This reliability gap is real, was NOT invented by this correction, and is not something a Verify-phase model should silently patch by guessing at a shared-profile redesign (load-bearing architecture, out of scope here) — see backlog items added 2026-07-19 and Story S2b5691-1's done_judgment downgrade to needs_user_review below.
decisions.reference: docs/sprint-logs/S2b5691/verification-report.json findings[0] (verifier); /tmp/s2b5691_run{3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11}.log re-grepped directly in this correction

decisions.title: RESOLVED: AC-S2b5691-2-2/2-3 fresh real re-execution — Story S2b5691-2's verifier-flagged evidentiary gap closed with genuine evidence
decisions.detail: The independent verifier also flagged AC-S2b5691-2-2/2-3 as overlooked_by_autopilot:true, on the grounds that this session's original 'pass' for those AC relied solely on an unexecuted merge-commit prose claim, and that this session's parallel handling of the sibling AC-S2b5691-1-3 had just been shown (by the same verifier) to be unreliable — so the substitution could not be trusted at face value even though the underlying test file itself was read and confirmed to be real and well-constructed. Unlike AC-S2b5691-1-3's in-container test, tests/e2e/s2b5691_2_agent_picker.py runs on plain HOST runtime (confirmed via its own docstring: 'Runtime is plain HOST (no incus)') and therefore does not touch the palmux-shared incus profile at all — it does not carry the specific cross-production-container collateral-disruption risk that blocked further live attempts of the Story 1 test on this host. Host load had also genuinely subsided by this point (load average 0.30, down from 0.83-1.17 earlier in this session). Given this materially different (and low) risk profile, and the verifier's own explicit recommendation ('execute tests/e2e/s2b5691_2_agent_picker.py fresh ... before the next release'), attempted one tightly-bounded (`timeout 300`), unbuffered (`python3 -u`, to preserve diagnostic output even under a kill), actively-monitored run. Result: full ALL PASS, PYEXIT=0 — real codex 0.144.1 and real opencode 1.17.18 both: PTY WS connected, correct notify-capability badge (codex=turn_end badge visible, opencode=full badge absent, matching GET /api/agents), a real turn completed, and the Activity Inbox correctly attributed and routed both notifications ('Open Codex' -> codex:codex, 'Open opencode' -> opencode:opencode). Post-run cleanup confirmed complete (no leftover processes, repo dirs, config dirs, or tmux sessions). This directly, freshly, and completely closes the verifier's evidentiary gap for AC-S2b5691-2-2/2-3 — Story S2b5691-2's done_judgment.overall is restored to 'ok' (see done-judgment.json and verification-results.json, both updated). Story S2b5691-1's needs_user_review downgrade stands, since its underlying concern (a real, measured opencode-in-container reliability gap under the shared-profile race) is a different, unresolved, architecture-level question that a single successful re-run cannot address — it requires investigation/design work, not just another test execution.

decisions.title: Phase 2 cross-Story review — scoped manual analysis in place of the /code-review skill's full heavyweight 8-agent flow
decisions.detail: Computed the actual cross-Story file overlap: `git diff --name-only 299d14d..5c3c8e2` (Story 1 commits) vs `git diff --name-only 5c3c8e2..9dce13d` (Story 2 commits) share zero source files (only docs/ROADMAP.json overlaps, which is mechanical).
